Recommendation.Description: Open the Global Manager UI (System, Location Manager) and check which Global Manager is active. If the active Global Manager is lost, follow the NSX Federation disaster recovery procedure and make the standby active.

Two Global Managers claim the active role. Do not change global configuration. Decide which Global Manager holds the valid configuration and force the other one to standby, as described in the NSX Federation recovery documentation.
Check that the Global Manager appliance is powered on and that the cloud proxy can reach it on TCP 443. If its certificate was replaced, update the trusted certificate of the adapter instance.

Deploy a standby Global Manager in another site and add it under System, Location Manager, Add Standby Global Manager. Without a standby the global configuration cannot be changed if the active Global Manager is lost.
The collection of this cycle is partial. Raise 'API call budget per manager and cycle' in the advanced settings of the adapter instance, or lengthen the collection interval.
Open System, Appliances on the manager and check the state of each node and service group. Restore or redeploy the failed node.
Configure a backup target and a schedule under System, Backup and Restore on the manager, then run a backup and confirm that it succeeds. A Global Manager can only be restored from its own backup.
Replace the certificate before it expires (System, Certificates). An expired manager certificate breaks the connection between the Global Manager and the Local Managers.

Check the network path between the active Global Manager and the Local Manager of this location (TCP 443 and 1236 in both directions) and the state of the Local Manager cluster. The location keeps forwarding traffic with its last configuration.
Check that the cloud proxy can reach the Local Manager on TCP 443 and that the account of the adapter instance is valid on this Local Manager. This is the monitoring path only.

The Local Manager presents a certificate that is not the one the Global Manager holds for it. Confirm the certificate change is expected, then update the location in the Global Manager so the thumbprint matches.
Open the location in System, Location Manager and read the sync status details. Start a full sync again from the Global Manager once the cause (connectivity, version, disk space) is fixed.

Check the RTEP network between the edge clusters of the locations: RTEP VLAN, MTU (1700 recommended), routing between RTEP subnets and the state of the edge nodes. Stretched segments and gateways depend on these sessions.
A version difference between the Global Manager and a location is expected only during an upgrade. Complete the upgrade so that all managers run a compatible version.
Check the connectivity between the two managers named on the channel (TCP 443 and 1236) and the state of both manager clusters.
Check the BGP neighbor on the Tier-0 gateway: interface state of the edge uplink, the peer router, AS numbers, passwords and timers.
The session is established but the peer advertises nothing. Check the routing policy and redistribution on the peer router.
Check the RTEP network between the two edge nodes of this tunnel: MTU on the whole path (1700 recommended), packet loss on the physical links and the load of the edge nodes.

Open the object in the Global Manager and read the error for each location of its span. Fix the cause (a missing edge cluster, an address conflict, a location that is not reachable), then save the object again.
Check the connectivity between the active and the standby Global Manager (ping, then TCP 443 and 1236) and the state of both Global Manager clusters.

Check the connectivity between the Global Manager and the location (ping, TCP 1236 in both directions) and that the async-replicator service runs on both sides (get service async_replicator). Its log is /var/log/async-replicator/ar.log.

Run get site-replicator remote-sites on the Local Managers to see the connection state between the locations, then check TCP 1236 between them. A location that is connected but not synchronized may still be electing its leader; check again after a few seconds.
Measure the round-trip time between the two managers named in the alarm. Federation supports up to 150 ms between locations; look for WAN congestion or a path change.
The sync queue grows when the remote location cannot keep up or cannot be reached. Check the connectivity to the remote location and /var/log/async-replicator/ar.log.
The location is in an inconsistent state. Delete the onboarding status of the location on the Global Manager, as the NSX alarm describes, then start the configuration import again.
Inter-site traffic on this tunnel is above the range VCF Operations learned for it. Check whether a migration, a backup or a replication job explains it before looking for a loop or a misrouted flow.

Open the object in the Global Manager and read the realization status for this location. Check the location alarms and the connection between the Global Manager and the location, then save the object again if needed.
